claim_boundary.supports: Kernel-checked for every glyph alphabet G, for a Lean restatement of the pinned restricted model (SnCarrier.lean sha256 357376de..., glyph alphabet abstracted, one-field wrappers flattened; clause-by-clause match with SnSyntax.lean and SnCarrierDischarge.unconstrainedSectionLift): the old-image law retr_n(sectionLift_n b) = accepted(b) for every base presentation at every stage, with an axiom report of propext only (the source old_image_base reports propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, which was confirmed by compiling the pinned files); the lift is injective; the base type has 1 + g + 3 g^2 elements for g = |G| and the image of the lift has that cardinality at every stage; the unrestricted (pre-repair) lift is not injective, admits no recovery with the old-image law, and sends the refusal token to the ground presentation; the declared table carrierCard never equals the base cardinality at stages 0, 2 and 3, equals it at stage 1 only for the empty alphabet, and cannot match the per-shape counts g and g^2 at stages 1 and 2 together; the index-zero carrier is empty, which is definitional (the table entry carrierCard 0 = 0 is itself a declaration, the same theorem as the source ground_carrier_empty). The per-stage shape counts [1, g, g^2, 2g^2] and the cumulative counts [1, 1+g, 1+g+g^2, 1+g+3g^2] used in the comparison are native-only (not stated in Lean); the Lean comparison is with the stage-independent total. Native: six alphabet sizes (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6) with explicit universes of up to 2764 presentations are built and the pinned lift/retraction executed: the old-image law holds on every stage-base pair (0 failures), lift image sizes equal 1+g+3g^2, the unrestricted lift collapses every non-base presentation onto the ground lift, the table matches the stage shape counts [1, g, g^2, 2g^2] at stages 1 and 3 only for g = 1 (so at the pairs (g = 1, stage 1) and (g = 1, stage 3), and at no other (g, stage) pair for g in {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6}), matches the cumulative counts nowhere except stage 1 of the empty alphabet, every stage guard is exact (S(S-1)|Base| mismatched-stage lifts refused) and glyph bodies of three or more glyphs are refused.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: A corrected cardinality theorem for the S(n) carriers: the table carrierCard remains a declared definition with no theorem relating Carrier n to the base presentations or the lift; off-image refusal completeness (node PG-SN-OFF-IMAGE-REFUSAL); nested lift, retraction or refusal terms as members of the base type; any theorem identifying the restatement with the pinned types at G = Glyph (36 letters and digits), and per-stage shape-count or cumulative-count statements in Lean (native-only); the real 36-glyph syntax beyond the instance baseCard 36 = 3925 and alphabets above six glyphs in the native certificate; wire parsing and the Python/Lean correspondence of the source; the locally defined UnrepairedCarrier of SnCarrierDischarge (a different type from Carrier); any physical, categorical or adjunction reading, including the string metadata of the custody-successor file mssn_functor_bridge.rs.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: For a Lean restatement of the pinned restricted S(n) model (SnCarrier.lean sha 357376de..., glyph alphabet abstracted, wrappers flattened), the base-presentation lift is injective with a left-inverse retraction at every stage and its image has 1+g+3g^2 points; the unrestricted lift has no recovery; the declared carrier table differs from the stage-independent base total 1+g+3g^2 at stages 0, 2 and 3 for every g (and at stage 1 unless g = 0), and no alphabet matches the per-shape counts g and g^2 at stages 1 and 2 together; the table is a declaration, not derived from the model.
claim_boundary.next_test: State and prove a corrected cardinality theorem: define Carrier n from the lift image or the stage-n shape set over the 36-glyph alphabet, prove its cardinality for n = 0..3 including the ground token, and decide whether carrierCard equals that derived function or must be replaced by it.

The advertised cardinalities are a declared table (carrierCard, docstring: declared, not source-derived), related to the lift by no theorem; the node bottleneck is therefore correct that they are not established, and this node shows that they differ from the cardinality the model has. The per-stage shape counts [1, g, g^2, 2g^2] and the cumulative counts [1, 1+g, 1+g+g^2, 1+g+3g^2] used in the comparison are native-only (not stated in Lean); the Lean comparison is with the stage-independent total.
